report.source_text: The patient was given acetazolamide, aspirin, ocular massage, and a combination of dorzolamide and timolol. She was monitored biweekly to assess visual acuity and intraocular pressure (IOP) for 12 weeks, followed by evaluations every 8 weeks for 6 months, then biannual check-ups for 2 years. At 6 weeks, after resolution of the preretinal hemorrhages, panretinal photocoagulation was performed to prevent neovascular glaucoma, which is associated with central retinal vein occlusion within 90 days. It was performed prophylactically as the patient resides in a remote area and was unwilling to adhere to a regular follow-up schedule. Intravitreal antivascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) was not used, as no macular edema was observed on OCT. By the 12th week, the patient’s vision was 6/36, with an IOP of 12 mmHg in the left eye.

clinician.final_diagnosis: central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) accompanied by ciliary retinal artery (CLRA) occlusion secondary to OCPs
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 28-year-old female presented with sudden, painless loss of vision in her left eye. Initial examination revealed severely reduced visual acuity (counting fingers at 0.5 feet) in the left eye. Fundoscopic examination showed signs of central retinal vein occlusion (optic disc edema, preretinal hemorrhages, venous dilation and tortuosity, cotton wool spots) and a white ischemic area suggestive of ciliary retinal artery occlusion. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) revealed inner retinal hyperreflectivity, and Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) showed delayed dye filling of the ciliary retinal artery. Extensive systemic workup for thrombophilia and other common risk factors (diabetes, hyperlipidemia, autoimmune conditions) was negative. Based on the clinical picture and exclusion of other causes, the patient was clinically diagnosed with CRVO and CLRA occlusion secondary to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs), which she had recently started. Treatment included acetazolamide, aspirin, ocular massage, dorzolamide and timolol, and panretinal photocoagulation. At 12 weeks, her vision improved to 6/36 in the left eye.
